correctness.rationale: Exact GP(n,2) closed-neighborhood GF2 equations give y_i=1+x_{i-1}+x_i+x_{i+1} and x_j+x_{j+1}+x_{j+5}+x_{j+6}=0, hence differences a_j=x_j+x_{j+1} are five-periodic and x has period <=10. Cyclic compatibility leaves 2/4 patterns if 5∤n, 32 if odd multiple of five, and 64 if 10|n. Five-period patterns have weights 3,5,7 with multiplicities 10,12,10; 32 twisted ten-period patterns have weight n. Independent 10-seed enumerator, corrected to deduplicate repeated seeds for n<10, reproduced each weight histogram for n=5..50. General theorem rests on recurrence and complete 32-pattern classification.

originality.rationale: The published same-family Lights Out literature treats homogeneous kernel nullity/weight structure; the submitted problem is the fixed nonzero-syndrome coset (I+A)s=1, whose weight enumerator is not determined by the homogeneous weight enumerator alone. Caro–Klostermeyer odd domination framework and Hatzl–Wagner generic parity algorithms do not evaluate this GP(n,2) affine coset; Wang–Zhang exact-one code problem is stricter, and similarly numbered induced-matching optimum counts edges rather than odd-dominating vertex subsets. Resultary yielded a separate GP(n,3) all-on result and differently defined GP(n,2) domination results, no earlier identical affine enumerator. Best-of-knowledge PASS, with old primary-source gaps.
residual_risks: Full historical literature on all-on Lights Out for generalized Petersen graphs was not exhaustively read, especially non-indexed tabulations.
Finite check n≤50 corroborates, but all n≥5 require algebraic recurrence; GP(n,k) for k≠2 is outside claim.
